messages.subject: Re: HMCMC
parts:
I'm familiar with Runge-Kutta methods (of which
the Euler method is a simple explicit instance)
because we use the leapfrog integrator in Stan.

The Euler method is described here:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_method

Given a simple diffeq w. initial value:

y'(t) = f(t,y(t)); y(t0) = y0

The algorithm (in pseudocode that's close to what the
real code would look like is):

euler(function y,
double y0,
double epsilon) {

yy[0] = y0;

tt[0] = 0;

for (n = 0; ; ++n) {

tt[n+1] = tt[n] + h;

yy[tt[n+1]] = yy[tt[n]] + epsilon * f(tt[n],yy[tt[n]]);

if (???) return yy[tt[n+1]]; // what is stop condition?

}
}

We can auto-dif the function Euler w.r.t. y0 or epsilon,
but I'm somehow guessing that you want the derivative of
something at the solution. But I have no idea how this all
fits together as part of a statistical model or how you'd go
about differentiating w.r.t. the return value.

- Bob

On 7/25/12 4:22 PM, Frederic Bois wrote:
> (bounced back because I cannot email stan-dev, resending:)
> OK.
> The stopping would be "if tt[n+1] >= final_time" (with simple
> provision not to over-shoot)
> Now, something is missing. We need to introduce parameters theta:
> y'(t) = f(t,y(t), theta); y(t0) = y0
>
> In the Bayesian numerical statistical inference problem you would aim
> at getting a sample
> of theta from their posterior, given a prior and data likelihood.
> Likelihood would be a
> function of y, and hence of theta (and possibly some more usual
> statistical parameters sigma...)
>
> So you would want the Jacobian of y w.r.t. theta at some points.
>
> There is no need to get the Jacobian of y' wrt y in that problem, only
> implicit (e.g. Gear's) integrators use that.
> My suggestion is just to use simple Euler (or RG) for getting Jac(y |
> theta), even if the actual integration is done with
> a more sophisticated (and stable) integrator (which might use Jac(y' |
> y), but that's a separate issue, even if synergistic in terms of
> computing speed is AD capability is available).
>
> FB
